verdict.headline: Weak hiring pulls short-term yields down, but long yields rise and the Nasdaq-100 hits a record
verdict.label: Close: S&P 500 7,722.72 (+0.73%), Nasdaq 27,190.86 (+1.19%), Nasdaq-100 30,825 (record), Dow +0.49%; payrolls +29,000, unemployment 4.2%; 2Y ~4.73% (-6 bp), 10Y ~5.28% (+4-5 bp), 30Y 5.629% (+2 bp); Oct hike odds ~20%; WTI $91.11, Brent $102.25; gold ~$4,217; BTC ~$84,500.
verdict.rationale_short: September payrolls rose 29,000, unemployment rose to 4.2% and wages rose 0.1%, and October hike odds fell to about 20% from about 35%. The two-year yield fell 6 basis points to 4.73%, but long yields reversed an early drop: the ten-year closed up about 4 basis points near 5.28% and the thirty-year rose 2 basis points to 5.629%, 1.5 basis points under its 2002 high, on a day WTI fell 1.9% on the G7 reserve release. The gap between two- and thirty-year yields widened to about 90 basis points, which is what the morning report said would mean the long-end pressure is not mainly about the Fed. Stocks followed the lower Fed path: the Nasdaq-100 closed at a record and the S&P 500 rose 0.73%. Whether Friday's long-end rise was positioning after Thursday's rally or a lasting demand for more yield cannot be told from one session. A thirty-year close above 5.644% would resume the rise; a close under 5.44% would say it is fading.
verdict.lede_short: US employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, and the odds of an October rate hike fell to about 20%. Short-term yields fell, but long-term yields rose anyway, with the 30-year at 5.629%, just under its 2002 high, while the Nasdaq-100 closed at a record. Weak hiring removed the Fed as the reason for high long yields; a 30-year close above 5.644% would resume the rise, and one under 5.44% would say it is fading.

supporting_data.label: Payrolls rose 29,000 in September, unemployment rose to 4.2% and hourly earnings rose 0.1% — weak hiring with slow wage growth removes the labour case for an October hike.

The ten-year rose almost 5 basis points to 5.281% and the thirty-year added 2 basis points to 5.629% after both fell on the release — lower Fed odds are not reaching long bonds, which sit 1.5 basis points under their 2002 high.
October hike odds fell to about 20% on CME FedWatch from about 35% before the report — the jobs data delayed the Fed path, with a December hike still widely priced.
The Nasdaq-100 rose 1.1% to a record 30,825 and the Russell 2000 gained 1.06% — stocks priced the lower hike odds and set aside a ten-year near its highest close since 2002.

The G7 agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude over four months, front-loading diesel — WTI fell 1.9% to $91.11 but Brent held near $102, so long yields rose on a day oil did not.

Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, about 25,000 above the 461,974 consensus, and its shares rose about 5% — a beat that weakens the case for broad consumer weakness after Nike's guide.

watchlist_mentions.note: Touched a record intraday high of $237.88 and closed at $233.95, up 1.34%, its first record since May, as lower hike odds lifted chips.
Rose about 5% after third-quarter deliveries of 486,532 beat the 461,974 consensus, though down 2.1% from a year earlier; results due October 21.
Rose about 3% as banks prepared a potential $60 billion financing package for AI chip infrastructure.
Near $84,500 in the evening, giving back the pre-payroll gain to about $86,460 even as stocks rallied.

trade_setups.thesis: The thirty-year rose 2 basis points to 5.629% on a payroll miss that cut October hike odds to about 20%, so the long-end pressure is coming from outside the Fed path; it sits 1.5 basis points under its 2002 high.
trade_setups.entry: Thirty-year 5.629% between the 2002 high of 5.644% above and 5.44% below.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close above 5.644% would resume the rise; a close under 5.44% would say Friday's rise was positioning.

trade_setups.thesis: The Nasdaq-100 set a record with the ten-year near 5.28%; chip valuations have absorbed higher long yields while hike odds fell.
trade_setups.entry: Ten-year ~5.28% against Thursday's intraday high of 5.344%; S&P 500 7,722.72 against Thursday's 7,666.45.
trade_setups.invalidation: A ten-year close above 5.344% with hike odds still low, or an S&P 500 close under 7,666.45, would test the gap.

trade_setups.thesis: Hiring slowed to 29,000 while manufacturing prices paid reached 77.9; ISM services prices decide whether a December hike stays priced.
trade_setups.entry: ISM services expected near 55.7 on Monday; manufacturing prices paid 77.9.
trade_setups.invalidation: A soft services prices index alongside weak payrolls would weaken the case for any further hike.
